lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Application or project: secured and unsecured debt

objective: Learners compare the interest cost of invented secured and unsecured borrowing of the same amount and connect the difference to collateral.
scenario: Ingrid is an invented seventh grader comparing two pretend loans of $4,000.00: a secured loan at 6% backed by the item purchased, and an unsecured loan at 19.5% with nothing pledged. All figures are invented.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Compute one simulated year of interest on Ingrid's invented secured loan at 6%.

prompts.text: How much interest does the secured loan cost in a year?

tasks.directions: Compute the unsecured loan at 19.5% for the same year, then find the annual gap between them.

prompts.text: How much interest does the unsecured loan cost in a year?
What is the annual difference between the two loans?

tasks.directions: Extend both loans to three simulated years on a simple-interest basis.

prompts.text: What does three years of the unsecured loan cost in interest?
How much more is that than three years of the secured loan?

tasks.directions: The cheaper loan carried a condition the dearer one did not.

prompts.text: Explain why Ingrid's secured loan costs so much less, and describe the risk the borrower accepts in exchange for that lower rate.

remediation: If a learner cannot see why the rates differ, ask what each lender can do if Ingrid stops paying, and derive the rate difference from those two answers.
extension: Ask the learner at what unsecured rate the two of Ingrid's loans would cost the same over three years, and to show the method.
